subject: How does the dsm function link the ddf.obj and the observation data?

messages.author: f2003e80c9e5162c
messages.subject: How does the dsm function link the ddf.obj and the observation data?
parts:
Hello Distance Samplers,

I'm working on a DSM to look at seabird habitat associations using R. I have a question about the mechanics of how the dsm function links observations to the detection function. I have a small number of observations for one species (n=49) and a larger number of detections of a second, similar species (n= ~250). Biologically, I think it is reasonable to lump the two species for fitting a combined detection function which I would then use for my dsm to estimate density of the rarer species.

My specific question is how the dsm function deals with observations in the detection function that are not linked through the object column to the observations data frame. The model runs but I'm struggling to figure out if it's actually doing what I hope it's doing. So, can I use observations in the detection function that I don't use in the observation data frame?

Any insights would be appreciated,
Brendan

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] How does the dsm function link the ddf.obj and the observation data?
parts:
Brendan

I don't have first-hand experience with what you are attempting to accomplish. I suspect the route to addressing your issue lies with taking the "multiddf" route.

The "ddf.obj" argument to the "dsm()" function can take a list of fitted detection function objects; in your case those could be detection functions for the different species. This way you need not make the assumption that the species share a common detection function.

This methodology is described in
  • Miller DL, Fifield D, Wakefield E, Sigourney DB. 2021. Extending density surface models to include multiple and double-observer survey data. PeerJ 9:e12113 https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.12113
The authors helpfully provide Rmarkdown vignettes of the analyses in the papers here:
  • All code and data are available at Zenodo: DL Miller. (2021). dill/multiddf-supp-materials: Code version for revision of the paper. (paper-revision). Zenodo. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5116140.
See if that approach may be useful to you.
